caption:
15% of your US dividends never make it into your TFSA. Here's what that box is actually good at, and what it quietly leaks.

A TFSA isn't an investment. It's a box you put investments inside. What grows in there is never taxed, and you don't pay a cent when you take it out. That's the win, and it's a big one.

The leak is US dividends. The US takes 15% on the way out, and Canada can't refund it because you don't owe tax here to claim it against. A $100 US dividend shows up as $85, every single time.

So the thing you expect to grow the most is what belongs in there. An RRSP is treated differently under the treaty, so look up your own case before you move anything.

One more that nobody says out loud: your room is counted in dollars, not shares. When prices drop, that same $7,000 buys more than it did last year. The catch is that a loss in a TFSA is just a loss, and you can't claim it on your taxes.

General education, not tax advice. Confirm your own numbers with CRA.

Save this and check your TFSA before your next buy.
